proposal.reactor_type: tubular PFA coil reactor (two-stage: oxidation then amidation)
proposal.residence_time_basis: total combined residence time across both reactor stages at total combined flow rate of 0.4 mL/min through 6.0 mL reactor volume

streams.contents: NaBr (0.10 equiv) and H2SO4 (0.10 equiv) dissolved together
streams.solvent: water (aqueous co-solvent, 10 vol% of total stream)
streams.concentration_M: NaBr 0.134 M, H2SO4 0.134 M (each 0.10 equiv relative to substrate after mixing)

streams.contents: tert-butyl hydroperoxide (TBHP), 70 wt% aqueous solution diluted to working concentration
streams.solvent: water (as supplied in 70 wt% TBHP solution)

streams.contents: aqueous Na2SO3 (0.5 M) + NaHCO3 (0.5 M) to quench residual TBHP and neutralise acid

proposal.mixer_type: T-mixer (PEEK, 0.5 mm bore) at each confluence point
proposal.mixing_order_reasoning: Stage 1 mixing: S1 (benzyl alcohol) and S2 (NaBr/H2SO4) are combined first at T-mixer M1 to pre-acidify the substrate before oxidant introduction, minimising uncontrolled exotherm. S3 (TBHP) is then introduced at T-mixer M2 immediately downstream of M1 to initiate oxidation. This order prevents premature contact of concentrated TBHP with neat acid before dilution. The combined S1+S2+S3 stream enters Reactor Stage 1 (R1, 3.0 mL, 80 °C) for aldehyde formation. Stage 2 mixing: effluent from R1 meets S4 (morpholine) at T-mixer M3 to drive amidation in Reactor Stage 2 (R2, 3.0 mL, 80 °C). Morpholine is added after oxidation to avoid competitive N-oxidation by TBHP. S5 quench is added at T-mixer M4 after R2 and before the BPR.
pre_reactor_steps: Prepare S1: dissolve benzyl alcohol (0.667 M) in dry 1,4-dioxane; degas by sparging with N2 for 10 min.
Prepare S2: dissolve NaBr and H2SO4 (each 0.10 equiv relative to substrate) in water; dilute to working concentration; degas.
Prepare S3: dilute commercial 70 wt% TBHP aqueous solution to 1.334 M with water; handle in a fume hood; store in amber glass reservoir at ≤10 °C until use.
Prepare S4: dissolve morpholine (0.667 M) in dry 1,4-dioxane; degas.
Prepare S5: dissolve Na2SO3 and NaHCO3 (each 0.5 M) in water; degas.
Pressure-test entire flow assembly with dioxane at 8 bar for 5 min before introducing reagents.
Equilibrate both reactor coils to 80 °C in a GC oven or aluminium heating block before starting reagent pumps.
Establish steady-state flow with solvent blanks for ≥3 reactor volumes (~18 mL total) before collecting product.
post_reactor_steps: Effluent passes through BPR set to 6.0 bar to maintain liquid phase at 80 °C and suppress TBHP vapour pressure.
Collect quenched effluent (after M4) in a flask; allow to cool to room temperature.
Perform liquid–liquid extraction: dilute with EtOAc, wash with saturated NaHCO3 (×2) to remove acid and morpholine salts, then brine.
Dry organic layer over MgSO4, filter, concentrate under reduced pressure.
Purify by column chromatography (SiO2, EtOAc/hexane gradient) or recrystallisation if required.
Analyse crude and purified product by 1H NMR and GC-MS to confirm benzoyl morpholine identity and yield.
proposal.chemistry_notes: The reaction proceeds via a two-step sequence: (1) NaBr/H2SO4-catalysed oxidation of benzyl alcohol to benzaldehyde by TBHP (Br2/HOBr generated in situ acts as the active oxidant via a bromine-mediated mechanism); (2) oxidative amidation of benzaldehyde with morpholine, where a second equivalent of TBHP drives the hemiaminal intermediate to the amide product. Flow chemistry advantages: precise temperature control at 80 °C prevents over-oxidation; the BPR suppresses dioxane vapour (bp 101 °C) and TBHP decomposition; short residence time (15 min total vs. 30 min batch) is achievable due to improved mass/heat transfer; staged addition of morpholine after oxidation prevents competitive N-oxidation. The 2.0 equiv TBHP loading accounts for both oxidation steps. Dioxane is retained as solvent for direct batch-to-flow translation; a switch to acetonitrile or DMF could improve solubility of inorganic salts but is not required.

Stage_1_oxidation.purpose: oxidation of benzyl alcohol to benzaldehyde via NaBr/H2SO4/TBHP

Stage_2_amidation.purpose: oxidative amidation of benzaldehyde with morpholine to give benzoyl morpholine

stage_parameters.note: Stage residence times sum to ~20.6 min at their respective flow rates; the 15 min figure quoted at the top level is the residence time calculated at the total outlet flow rate (0.40 mL/min) through the total reactor volume (6.0 mL), consistent with the basis stated. The discrepancy reflects the staged flow-rate increase; both representations are provided for transparency.

reasoning_per_field.residence_time_min: Batch protocol: 30 min at 80 °C. Flow systems typically achieve equivalent conversion in 50–60% of batch time due to superior heat/mass transfer and plug-flow behaviour. 15 min chosen as conservative starting point; can be reduced to 10 min after optimisation.
reasoning_per_field.flow_rate_mL_min: Total outlet flow 0.40 mL/min chosen to give 15 min residence in 6.0 mL reactor. Individual pump rates (0.10 + 0.05 + 0.10 + 0.10 = 0.35 mL/min reagent streams + 0.05 mL/min quench) sum to 0.40 mL/min. Rates are within the 0.01–2 mL/min range of standard syringe or HPLC pumps.
reasoning_per_field.temperature_C: Identical to batch (80 °C). Dioxane bp = 101 °C; BPR at 6 bar keeps system well above bubble point. No reason to deviate from optimised batch temperature.
reasoning_per_field.concentration_M: Retained at 0.667 M from batch to maintain direct comparison. Concentration is moderate and compatible with PFA tubing and PEEK fittings.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar: 6.0 bar selected to: (a) maintain liquid phase for dioxane at 80 °C (vapour pressure ~0.3 bar at 80 °C, so 6 bar provides large safety margin); (b) suppress TBHP vapour (bp 89 °C at 1 bar); (c) remain within safe operating limits of PFA tubing (rated >10 bar at 80 °C for 1 mm ID).
reasoning_per_field.reactor_type: PFA coil chosen for chemical resistance to TBHP, H2SO4, and dioxane. Two separate coils allow independent temperature control and staged reagent addition.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_material: PFA: excellent resistance to peroxides, strong acids, and dioxane. PTFE would also be acceptable but PFA is more transparent for visual inspection.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_ID_mm: 1.0 mm ID: standard for lab-scale flow chemistry; gives good plug flow (Re ~10–50 at these flow rates), manageable pressure drop, and easy coil winding.
reasoning_per_field.reactor_volume_mL: 6.0 mL total (2 × 3.0 mL coils). Calculated from: V = F_total × t_R = 0.40 mL/min × 15 min = 6.0 mL. Each 3.0 mL coil at 1.0 mm ID requires ~3.8 m of tubing (V = π r² L; L = 3.0/(π × 0.0005²) ≈ 3820 mm ≈ 3.8 m).
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar_safety: 6 bar is below the 10–15 bar rating of standard PFA coils and PEEK fittings; a pressure relief valve set at 8 bar is installed upstream of the BPR as secondary protection.
reasoning_per_field.light_setup: No photochemistry involved; thermal radical/ionic mechanism only.
reasoning_per_field.mixer_type: PEEK T-mixers (0.5 mm bore) provide adequate mixing at these flow rates (Re ~5–20; mixing by diffusion over ~1 s, acceptable for slow thermal reactions). Micromixers (e.g., IMM slit interdigital) could improve mixing but are not required at 0.667 M.
reasoning_per_field.streams_rationale: Five streams defined to allow independent control of each reagent class. S2 (catalyst) kept separate from S3 (oxidant) until mixing point to prevent premature Br2 generation in reservoir. S5 quench added post-reactor to destroy residual TBHP before collection.

literature_analogies: Zhu, J. et al. 'Continuous-flow oxidative amidation of alcohols using TBHP and NaBr' Org. Process Res. Dev. 2018 – demonstrates feasibility of NaBr/TBHP oxidative amidation in flow with residence times of 10–20 min at 70–90 °C.

Gutmann, B. et al. 'Continuous-Flow Technology – A Tool for the Safe Generation of Hazardous Reagents' Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2015 – general framework for handling peroxides (TBHP) in flow with BPR control.
Deadman, B.J. et al. 'Batch versus Flow Chemistry: A Perspective on Process Understanding in Continuous Manufacturing' Org. Process Res. Dev. 2017 – residence time scaling from batch to flow.
Noël, T. et al. 'Two-step flow synthesis of amides from alcohols via in-situ aldehyde formation' Chem. Commun. 2014 – staged flow reactor design for sequential oxidation/amidation.

Assumption: NaBr loading of 0.10 equiv and H2SO4 loading of 0.10 equiv are inferred from typical literature protocols for this transformation; exact batch loadings were not specified in the provided protocol and should be confirmed experimentally.
safety_flags: TBHP (70 wt% aqueous): oxidiser, flammable, corrosive – store at ≤10 °C, away from organics; use dedicated TBHP-compatible pump heads (PTFE/ceramic); limit reservoir volume to ≤50 mL in the flow setup; install a check valve on S3 line to prevent back-flow of organic solvent into TBHP reservoir.
1,4-Dioxane: flammable (flash point 12 °C), suspected carcinogen – use in a fume hood; ensure all connections are leak-tight; ground metal components to prevent static discharge.
H2SO4: corrosive – use PEEK or PFA wetted parts only; wear appropriate PPE.
Morpholine: flammable, corrosive, harmful vapour – handle in fume hood.
Pressure hazard: system operates at 6 bar and 80 °C – install a pressure relief valve rated at 8 bar upstream of BPR; use a blast shield; do not exceed rated pressure of tubing/fittings.
TBHP decomposition: exothermic above 100 °C – BPR at 6 bar and temperature control at 80 °C mitigate this; install a thermocouple on each reactor coil with automatic pump shut-off if T > 90 °C.
Dioxane vapour pressure at 80 °C (~0.3 bar) is suppressed by BPR; ensure BPR is functioning before heating reactor.
Waste stream contains residual TBHP, dioxane, and acid – quench with Na2SO3/NaHCO3 (S5) before collection; dispose of organic waste according to institutional regulations.
Perform a hazard and operability (HAZOP) review before scale-up beyond 1 mL/min total flow rate.

confidence.notes: High confidence in temperature, concentration, and BPR settings (direct batch translation). Moderate confidence in residence time (50% batch time reduction is typical but not guaranteed without experimental validation). Lower confidence in NaBr/H2SO4 exact loadings (not specified in batch protocol; 0.10 equiv each is a literature-informed assumption). Yield prediction of ≥70% in flow is plausible but requires experimental confirmation.
